newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bill would ban Arabs from top job in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Bill would ban Arabs from top job in Israel.

text.p: A member of Israel's right-wing coalition proposed on Sunday barring Arabs from ever running for prime minister of the Jewish state.
Lawmaker Michael Kleiner's proposal would make Israel's most powerful office off-limits to the country's 850,000 Arab citizens who make up about 18 percent of the population.
"Every non-Jewish citizen can...do any job except for the job of prime minister who represents, symbolises and expresses the substance of the state as the state of the Jews," he told Israel Radio.
Azmi Bishara, an Israeli Arab member of parliament, said the bill aimed to torpedo his own announced candidacy for the top job in national elections more than three years away.

"I am a citizen of the state of Israel first of all," Bishara told Israel Radio. "I know I won't be elected prime minister...I believe that running for the prime ministership is a way to politically influence the process.

"The time has come for the unusual, abnormal state of Israel...to start undergoing a normalisation...and get used to an Arab citizen taking his citizenship seriously, standing for election, receiving five, six or seven percent -- it's not important -- but to try to influence things," Bishara told army radio.
Israel's Declaration of Independence, adopted with the state's creation in 1948, promises equal social and political rights for all inhabitants irrespective of religion, race or sex.
Kleiner, a member of the ruling Likud-Gesher-Tsomet bloc, said his proposal would require that all candidates for prime minister be Jews who have resided in Israel for at least seven years.
"Even in England the king can only be an Anglican," Kleiner said.
